_comment: Citations for the terrain-realism substrate (code/sim/los.py) and its two gates: SWEG_TERRAIN_COLLISION (movement may not cross a Ruin/Impassable wall; INFANTRY/BEASTS excepted per the 10e Ruins movement rule) and SWEG_TERRAIN_LOS (shooting target legality requires line of sight; Indirect Fire excepted). The line-of-sight OCCLUSION rule itself is already cited under terrain.ruin_infantry_los and simulator.towering_los in core_terrain_ruins.json — the substrate delegates its has_los to code.map.Map.has_line_of_sight, so those citations remain the source of truth for what blocks a sightline. See docs/TERRAIN_REALISM_PROPOSAL.md.

simulator.terrain_wall_collision.quoted_text: Models cannot move through the walls of this terrain feature (though they can move through any door or window openings that are large enough to accommodate their base). INFANTRY, BEASTS, IMPERIUM PRIMARCH, and BELISARIUS CAWL models can move through this terrain feature's walls, floors and ceilings as if they were not there.
simulator.terrain_wall_collision.trigger: a non-FLY model's straight move segment would cross a RUIN or IMPASSABLE terrain rectangle whose interior contains neither its start point (env-gated SWEG_TERRAIN_COLLISION=1), and the model is NOT an INFANTRY or BEAST model (which move through ruin walls as if they were not there)
simulator.terrain_wall_collision.effect: The move is clamped to the near face of the first wall the segment crosses (code.sim.los.wall_clamp) instead of tunnelling through it, and candidate-destination pickers in code.sim.geometry._move_toward reject wall-crossing candidates when unblocked ones exist (closing open issue 52 — units path point-to-point through ruin walls). FLY movers pass over terrain and are never terrain-blocked; INFANTRY/BEAST movers move through ruin walls (block_ruins=False) but are still stopped by IMPASSABLE terrain; every other mover is stopped by both RUIN and IMPASSABLE. OBSCURING (Woods) and cover pieces are passable and never block movement. The mover already standing inside a wall may leave it. Byte-identical when SWEG_TERRAIN_COLLISION is unset (the gate is default-off; no caller sets the terrain-block flag, so _move_toward runs its exact pre-existing path). Wahapedia core Ruins movement rule; INFANTRY/BEAST exception verbatim.

simulator.terrain_los_gate.rule_name: Ruins (Line of Sight) — shooting target legality
simulator.terrain_los_gate.quoted_text: Models cannot see over or through this terrain feature. AIRCRAFT models are exceptions to this - visibility to and from such models is determined normally, even if this terrain feature is wholly in between them and the observing model. Models can see into this terrain feature normally, and models that are wholly within this terrain feature can see out of it normally.
simulator.terrain_los_gate.trigger: a ranged attacker selects targets in code.simulator.Battle._do_shoot / Fire Overwatch, env-gated SWEG_TERRAIN_LOS=1: an enemy unit is a legal target only if it is visible (a straight sightline from the attacker is not blocked by a Ruin/Woods wall wholly between them), unless the attacker's weapon has Indirect Fire (weapon.indirect_fire), which may target units it cannot see (at -1 to Hit, per the Indirect Fire core rule)
simulator.terrain_los_gate.effect: Occluded enemy units are removed from the legal-target pool, routing the check through the shared substrate code.sim.los.has_los (which delegates to code.map.Map.has_line_of_sight — the AIRCRAFT/TOWERING/endpoint-contained exceptions are cited under terrain.ruin_infantry_los and simulator.towering_los). Benefit of Cover keeps its existing positional grant (code.map.Map.cover_at), unchanged. This makes shooting resolution and the future threat-projection planner (docs/THREAT_LAYER_PROPOSAL.md, docs/TERRAIN_REALISM_PROPOSAL.md Stage T4) read one occlusion geometry. Byte-identical when SWEG_TERRAIN_LOS is unset: the pre-existing Battle._do_shoot / _fire_overwatch line-of-sight legality check (which already denied ~45% of candidate shots on a dense map) runs unchanged via Map.has_line_of_sight; with the gate set the identical result flows through los.has_los.
